questions.stem: The long fibre that carries an impulse away from the cell body of a neurone is the
questions.explanation: The axon is the outgoing fibre. Dendrites bring impulses in; the synapse is the gap to the next cell; myelin is the insulating sheath wrapped around many axons, not the fibre itself.

distractorRationale.a: Dendrites receive impulses and pass them towards the cell body
distractorRationale.c: A synapse is a gap, not a fibre
distractorRationale.d: Myelin is insulation around the axon

questions.stem: The central nervous system consists of the
questions.explanation: By definition the CNS is the brain plus the spinal cord. Cranial and spinal nerves make up the peripheral nervous system. Sense organs are receptors; muscles and glands are effectors.

distractorRationale.b: Those nerves are the peripheral nervous system
distractorRationale.c: Sense organs detect stimuli but are not the CNS
distractorRationale.d: Muscles and glands are effectors at the end of a pathway

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Nervous System and Sense Organs

questions.stem: In a spinal reflex, the correct order of structures is

options.text: effector → motor neurone → receptor → sensory neurone
receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone in the spinal cord → motor neurone → effector
receptor → motor neurone → brain → sensory neurone → effector

questions.explanation: The impulse starts at the receptor, travels in on a sensory neurone, crosses synapses in the spinal cord via a relay neurone, and leaves on a motor neurone to the effector. The brain is informed but is not required for the arc itself, which is why the response is so fast.

distractorRationale.a: This sequence runs the wrong way, from effector to receptor
distractorRationale.c: The motor neurone is last, not second, and a spinal reflex does not have to go through the brain
distractorRationale.d: The brain does not start a simple withdrawal reflex

questions.stem: When the eye focuses on a near object, the

options.text: ciliary muscles relax, suspensory ligaments become taut and the lens thins
ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments slacken and the lens becomes fatter

questions.explanation: Accommodation for near vision needs a more convex lens. Contraction of the ciliary muscle reduces tension in the suspensory ligaments, so the elastic lens bulges. The opposite set of changes is used for distant objects. The iris controls light intensity, not focal length.

distractorRationale.a: This is accommodation for a distant object, not a near one
distractorRationale.c: The pupil never closes completely in normal vision; the iris does not focus the image
distractorRationale.d: The optic nerve transmits impulses; it does not change length to focus

questions.stem: The part of the ear that converts sound vibrations into nerve impulses is the
questions.explanation: Hair cells in the organ of Corti inside the cochlea transduce vibration into electrical impulses that travel in the auditory nerve. The pinna and tympanum only collect and transmit sound; the semicircular canals detect rotational movement for balance, not sound.

distractorRationale.a: The pinna funnels sound into the canal; it does not generate impulses
distractorRationale.b: The tympanum vibrates but does not convert the vibration into a nerve impulse
distractorRationale.d: Semicircular canals serve balance, not hearing

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Nervous System and Sense Organs

questions.stem: Rods differ from cones in that rods

options.text: detect colour in bright light and are concentrated at the fovea
function in dim light and do not distinguish colour
are found only in the blind spot

questions.explanation: Rods are highly sensitive, so they work in moonlight and at dusk, but they give only shades of grey. Cones need bright light, detect colour and are packed at the fovea. The blind spot has neither rods nor cones, which is why an image falling there is not seen.

distractorRationale.a: This describes cones, not rods
distractorRationale.c: The optic nerve is formed by axons of ganglion cells, not by rods themselves
distractorRationale.d: The blind spot has no photoreceptors at all

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Nervous System and Sense Organs

questions.stem: A drug that blocks the release of transmitter at synapses in the spinal cord would most directly prevent

options.text: detection of a stimulus by a skin receptor
passage of the impulse from a sensory neurone to a motor neurone in a reflex
refraction of light by the cornea

questions.explanation: A reflex depends on chemical transmission across spinal synapses. If transmitter cannot be released, the sensory neurone still fires but the relay and motor neurones are not stimulated, so the effector never receives the command. Axonal conduction and receptors do not use that synaptic transmitter step.

distractorRationale.a: Receptors start the impulse before any synapse in the cord is involved
distractorRationale.c: Myelin speeds axonal conduction electrically; it is not the synaptic chemical step
distractorRationale.d: The cornea is part of the eye's optics, unrelated to spinal synapses

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Nervous System and Sense Organs

questions.stem: A patient hears well but cannot keep balance when walking in the dark. Which structures are most likely damaged?
questions.explanation: Hearing is intact, so the cochlea, tympanum and ossicles are working. Balance in the dark depends on the semicircular canals (and related vestibular organs), because vision cannot then compensate. Cones affect colour vision in bright light, not body equilibrium.

distractorRationale.a: Cochlear damage would impair hearing, which this patient has not lost
distractorRationale.c: Damage here would reduce hearing by blocking sound transmission
distractorRationale.d: Cones are photoreceptors; they do not maintain balance

questions.stem: Which part of the neurone is responsible for receiving signals from other neurones?
questions.explanation: Dendrites are the extensions of a neurone that receive signals from other neurones. They play a crucial role in transmitting information to the cell body.

distractorRationale.a: The axon transmits impulses away from the cell body, not towards it.
distractorRationale.c: The cell body integrates signals but does not receive them directly.
distractorRationale.d: The myelin sheath insulates the axon and speeds up impulse transmission, but does not receive signals.

questions.stem: The function of the myelin sheath in a neurone is to

options.text: Increase the speed of impulse transmission

questions.explanation: The myelin sheath acts as an insulator for the axon, allowing electrical impulses to transmit more quickly along the neurone through a process called saltatory conduction.

distractorRationale.a: While the myelin sheath does provide some protection, its primary role is not protective.
distractorRationale.c: Neurotransmitters are stored in synaptic vesicles, not in the myelin sheath.
distractorRationale.d: Regeneration of axons is not a function of the myelin sheath; it mainly facilitates faster impulse transmission.

questions.stem: The part of the brain responsible for coordinating voluntary movements is the
questions.explanation: The cerebellum is responsible for the coordination of voluntary movements and balance. It helps in fine-tuning motor activity and maintaining posture.

distractorRationale.a: The cerebrum is involved in higher brain functions, such as thought and action, but not specifically in coordination.
distractorRationale.c: The brainstem controls basic life functions, such as breathing, not voluntary movements.
distractorRationale.d: The thalamus acts as a relay station for sensory information, but does not coordinate movements.

questions.stem: In the reflex arc, which structure is responsible for carrying the impulse from the spinal cord to the effector?
questions.explanation: The motor neurone carries the impulse from the spinal cord to the effector, which could be a muscle or gland that responds to the reflex action.

distractorRationale.a: The sensory neurone carries the impulse from the receptor to the spinal cord, not to the effector.
distractorRationale.c: Interneurons are involved in processing the signal within the spinal cord but do not directly activate the effector.
distractorRationale.d: The cerebellum is involved in coordination but does not play a role in the reflex arc pathway.

questions.stem: Which part of the eye is responsible for controlling the amount of light that enters?
questions.explanation: The pupil is the opening in the center of the iris that regulates the amount of light entering the eye. It constricts in bright light and dilates in low light.

distractorRationale.a: The cornea helps to focus light but does not control the amount of light entering the eye.
distractorRationale.c: The lens focuses light onto the retina but does not regulate light entry.
distractorRationale.d: The retina detects light but is not involved in controlling its entry.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the rods in the human eye?
questions.explanation: Rods are photoreceptor cells in the retina that are highly sensitive to light, allowing for vision in low-light conditions, which is referred to as night vision.

distractorRationale.a: Color vision is primarily the function of cones, not rods.
distractorRationale.b: While rods contribute to peripheral vision, their main role is in low-light conditions.
distractorRationale.d: Sharp vision is mainly the function of cones, which provide detailed and color vision.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: Which structure in the ear is responsible for maintaining balance?
questions.explanation: The semicircular canals are part of the inner ear and are essential for maintaining balance and spatial orientation. They detect rotational movements of the head.

distractorRationale.a: The cochlea is involved in hearing, not balance.
distractorRationale.c: The auditory canal transmits sound waves to the eardrum, but has no role in balance.
distractorRationale.d: The Eustachian tube helps equalize pressure but does not maintain balance.

questions.stem: The part of the eye that focuses light onto the retina is the
questions.explanation: The lens is a transparent structure that adjusts its shape to focus light onto the retina, allowing for clear vision at various distances.

distractorRationale.a: The cornea does help to focus light, but the lens fine-tunes this focus.
distractorRationale.c: The iris controls the size of the pupil but does not focus light.
distractorRationale.d: The sclera provides protection and shape to the eye but is not involved in focusing light.

questions.stem: Which part of the ear is involved in the conversion of sound waves into mechanical vibrations?
questions.explanation: The tympanic membrane, also known as the eardrum, vibrates when sound waves hit it, converting sound waves into mechanical vibrations that are transmitted to the inner ear.

distractorRationale.a: The auricle collects sound waves but does not convert them into vibrations.
distractorRationale.c: The oval window transmits vibrations to the cochlea but is not the initial site of conversion.
distractorRationale.d: The Eustachian tube equalizes pressure but has no role in sound conversion.

questions.stem: The reflex action is an example of which type of response?
questions.explanation: A reflex action is an involuntary response to a stimulus, meaning it occurs without conscious thought and is usually very quick.

distractorRationale.a: Voluntary responses require conscious thought and control, unlike reflex actions.
distractorRationale.c: Conscious responses involve awareness and decision-making, which does not apply to reflexes.
distractorRationale.d: A delayed response is not characteristic of reflex actions, which are immediate.

questions.stem: Which type of neurone carries impulses from the sensory organs to the central nervous system?
questions.explanation: Sensory neurones transmit impulses from sensory receptors to the central nervous system, allowing the body to respond to external stimuli.

distractorRationale.a: Motor neurones carry impulses away from the CNS to effectors, not towards it.
distractorRationale.c: Interneurons connect sensory and motor neurones within the CNS but do not carry impulses from sensory organs.
distractorRationale.d: Efferent neurones are another term for motor neurones, which do not carry impulses from sensory organs.

questions.stem: The main function of the dendrites in a neurone is to

options.text: carry impulses away from the cell body

questions.explanation: Dendrites are the branched extensions of a neurone that receive signals from other neurones. They play a crucial role in transmitting information to the cell body for processing.

distractorRationale.a: This option describes the function of the axon, not the dendrites.
distractorRationale.c: Insulation is the function of the myelin sheath, not the dendrites.
distractorRationale.d: Dendrites do not transmit impulses to muscles; they receive signals.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is primarily responsible for the processing of visual information?
questions.explanation: The retina contains photoreceptor cells that convert light into neural signals, which are then processed by the brain. It plays a critical role in vision.

distractorRationale.a: The cornea helps to focus light but does not process visual information.
distractorRationale.c: The optic nerve transmits visual information but does not process it.
distractorRationale.d: The lens focuses light onto the retina but does not process the information.

questions.stem: Which part of the ear is responsible for amplifying sound vibrations?
questions.explanation: The ossicles, which include the malleus, incus, and stapes, are small bones in the middle ear that amplify sound vibrations before they reach the cochlea.

distractorRationale.a: The cochlea converts sound vibrations into nerve impulses, but it does not amplify them.
distractorRationale.b: The eardrum vibrates in response to sound but does not amplify the sound.
distractorRationale.d: The auditory canal transmits sound to the eardrum but does not amplify it.

questions.stem: Which type of neurone is responsible for transmitting impulses from the central nervous system to effectors?
questions.explanation: Motor neurones carry impulses away from the central nervous system to effectors such as muscles and glands, facilitating response actions.

distractorRationale.a: Sensory neurones carry impulses from sensory organs to the central nervous system.
distractorRationale.c: Interneurones connect sensory and motor neurones within the central nervous system.
distractorRationale.d: Afferent neurones are another term for sensory neurones.

questions.stem: What is the function of the vitreous humor in the eye?

options.text: To focus light onto the retina
To maintain the shape of the eyeball

questions.explanation: The vitreous humor is a gel-like substance that helps maintain the shape of the eyeball and provides support to the retina.

distractorRationale.a: The lens focuses light onto the retina, not the vitreous humor.
distractorRationale.c: The vitreous humor does not absorb light; its primary role is structural.
distractorRationale.d: The lens is protected by the cornea and aqueous humor, not the vitreous humor.

questions.stem: The blind spot in the eye is located where

options.text: the optic nerve exits the retina
light is focused on the retina

questions.explanation: The blind spot is the area on the retina where the optic nerve exits the eye, and it lacks photoreceptors, resulting in no visual information being detected.

distractorRationale.b: The area where light is focused on the retina is the fovea, not the blind spot.
distractorRationale.c: The cornea is at the front of the eye and does not relate to the blind spot.
distractorRationale.d: The lens focuses light but is not related to the blind spot.

questions.stem: Which part of the nervous system controls involuntary actions?
questions.explanation: The autonomic nervous system regulates involuntary functions such as heart rate, digestion, and respiratory rate, operating without conscious control.

distractorRationale.a: The central nervous system processes information but does not directly control actions.
distractorRationale.b: The peripheral nervous system includes both voluntary and involuntary pathways.

questions.explanation: The cochlea contains hair cells that transduce sound waves into electrical signals, which are then sent to the brain for interpretation.

questions.stem: Which type of receptor in the eye is primarily responsible for color vision?
questions.explanation: Cones are photoreceptor cells in the retina that are responsible for color vision and function best in bright light. They allow us to perceive a wide range of colors due to their sensitivity to different wavelengths of light.

distractorRationale.a: Rods are more sensitive to light but do not detect color.
distractorRationale.c: Bipolar cells are intermediaries in the visual pathway but do not detect light themselves.

questions.stem: What is the role of the synapse in the nervous system?
questions.explanation: The synapse is a junction between two neurones where neurotransmitters are released to transmit nerve impulses. This process is crucial for communication within the nervous system and allows for the propagation of signals from one neurone to another.

distractorRationale.b: Action potentials are generated along the neurone, not at the synapse.
distractorRationale.c: While neurotransmitters are stored in vesicles, the primary function of the synapse is not storage but transmission.
distractorRationale.d: Insulation of neurones is provided by the myelin sheath, not the synapse.
